evals.prompt: Plan conversion of a scanned expense form with a three-column attendee table, blank company cells and checked/unchecked boxes. The document has no text layer. Semantic accuracy matters. State the first candidate tool, acceptance checks and targeted fallback; do not execute conversion for this routing evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Choose a structural candidate rather than unconditionally run plain OCR; retain empty cells and verify selections from source images. Escalate unresolved regions to approved vision, not a public endpoint.
assertions: Uses structural parsing for the printed form
Preserves source cell placement and blank fields
Keeps vision within the approved data boundary

evals.prompt: A PDF conversion command exits 0 and the structural Markdown checker passes. OCR confidence is high, but the receipt output omits its VAT rows and a company appears under the wrong attendee. The source shows 12,00 on the form and 12,01 on the receipt. May I publish it, and what should happen next? Do not execute tools for this routing evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Reject semantic acceptance, name relationship/coverage failures, verify source values without reconciling the different totals, and reprocess only failed regions. Structural success and model confidence cannot certify meaning.
assertions: Does not accept exit 0 or structural checks as semantic proof
Targets the failed regions rather than blindly runs all engines
Flags unresolved readings instead of inventing repairs

evals.prompt: Convert a short, clean single-column digital PDF to Markdown on a Windows laptop. Its text and paragraph order are intact. Explain the minimal route and the final check, without installing models or executing conversion for this routing evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Use native extraction without unnecessary OCR/Docling/MinerU/vision; check source fidelity before completion. No macOS-only engine or resource-heavy ladder is necessary.
assertions: Does not unnecessarily OCR or run a model ladder
Still checks the output against source
